data.body:
Patchset 2 pushed to change 2623. Both -1 votes were cleared by the push; gates are
re-running. NOT submitted, ticket deliberately left in_progress.

## Verified -1: fixed by REBASE, as diagnosed — no recheck

Rebased onto origin/main (ee2c54f881d6), which carries c57057f41's grounding-terraform
extra. Confirmed the mechanism directly: `git show ee2c54f881d6:pyproject.toml | grep -c
grounding-terraform` returns 1 where the old parent 3ae5c7a6082c returned 0. Change-Id
Iac326411 preserved throughout (amended with `git commit --amend --no-edit` and
`make amend-msg`), so this is patchset 2 of 2623, not a duplicate change.

Same drift bit the local venv, incidentally, and is worth recording as the n=3 the previous
comment was waiting for: this worktree's .venv predates the extra, so
tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_plan_review_tools.py fails locally with
`assert 'abstain' == 'refuted'` purely because python-hcl2 is absent. It passes after
`uv pip install python-hcl2==8.1.3`. Environment, not code — but the failure text names
neither the missing module nor the extra, so it reads as a logic bug.

## LLM-Review -1: the reviewer was RIGHT that the sides did not span the same bytes, and
## WRONG about why — which changes the fix

The reviewer's stated mechanism was "BuildKit build cache lives under
/var/lib/docker/buildkit, NOT under overlay2". Verified against moby source rather than
accepted: it does not hold for this daemon. In the classic graphdriver configuration
`builder/builder-next/controller.go`'s `newGraphDriverController` hands the LIVE
`GraphDriver` and `LayerStore` to `snapshot.NewSnapshotter`, and every snapshot operation
delegates — `Prepare` -> `GraphDriver.Create`, `Mounts` -> `GraphDriver.Get`, `Usage` ->
`GraphDriver.DiffSize`. So BuildKit's cache snapshots ARE inside overlay2; `.../buildkit/`
holds the metadata DBs plus a content store, of which only `content/` is routinely GB-sized.

That matters because it rules out one of the two candidate fixes. NARROWING THE LEDGER TO
IMAGES + CONTAINERS WOULD HAVE BEEN ACTIVELY WRONG: it would republish a fully prunable
build cache as "bytes prune cannot reach" and page, against a 2 GiB threshold, on every
build. WIDENING THE `du` TO overlay2 + buildkit was also rejected — it patches the symptom
with a directory list, and it still breaks outright under the containerd snapshotter, where
the layer bytes are under `.../containerd/` and overlay2 goes stale, pegging the residue at
its clamp forever on a box that is filling.

DIRECTION CHOSEN: widen BOTH sides to the same layout-independent set — a `du -sx` of the
WHOLE Docker root against ALL FOUR ledger rows, Local Volumes included. The residue then
answers one question that no storage-driver detail can move: how much of what dockerd is
storing does dockerd itself not know about. It also picks up consumers NO ledger row covers
— container JSON logs under `.../containers/<id>/`, BuildKit's content store, the layer
metadata under `.../image/` — each of which can fill root while `docker system df` reports a
comfortable total, which is precisely the incident shape.

Honest residual, written into the code: a Docker root split across mounts would under-report,
because `-x` stops the `du` at the boundary while the ledger keeps counting. That direction
loses sensitivity rather than inventing a page, and it is not this box.

TWO TESTS PIN THE CHOICE, each failing under one of the rejected alternatives:
 - test_a_build_cache_is_not_reported_as_unreachable_residue — under the narrowed ledger it
   fails `assert 4000000000 == 0` (a 4 GB prunable cache published as unreachable residue).
 - test_the_residue_survives_a_daemon_that_stores_layers_outside_overlay2 — replays the
   containerd-snapshotter shape; under patchset 1 AND under the widened-`du` variant it fails
   `assert 0 == 7.7 GiB`, i.e. the metric reads perfectly healthy on a filling box.
RED against patchset 1's observability.sh: 7 failed / 15 passed. RED against a
narrowed-ledger variant: 3 failed.

## The alarm is renamed

rebar-docker-unaccounted-overlay2 -> rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes, because the metric is no
longer scoped to one subdirectory and a name that says otherwise is the next reader's wrong
turn. Terraform, the runbook table and the alarm guard's watched set all follow.

## The five advisories, all addressed

 - docker-storage-cap.sh:251 (the important one — absence of execution reported as success,
   4th instance). `systemctl reload docker` is GONE, not merely re-worded: SIGHUP applies a
   fixed key set that excludes builder.gc, so its zero exit was the only evidence the script
   had for claiming "in effect". Activation is now OBSERVED — the mtime of `/proc/<MainPID>`
   (which the kernel sets at process creation) against the mtime of daemon.json — and it FAILS
   CLOSED: undeterminable reports NOT in effect. Three distinguishable messages, all tested,
   and the runbook now carries the message-to-action table. The install path will now always
   and correctly say NOT in effect against a live daemon, which is the truth it was hiding.
 - docker-storage-cap.sh:235 — backups bounded to the 5 most recent, pruned oldest-first on
   every install. A disk-ceiling script must not grow an unbounded on-disk set of its own.
 - observability.sh:318 — both percent gauges clamped to 100; the unclamped *_bytes gauges
   beside them carry the magnitude and the 85 threshold is unaffected.
 - test_docker_storage_cap.py:397-411 — the change-detector is gone. BOTH compose-up
   assertions now RUN the boot orchestrator over stubs and read the order the steps actually
   executed in. Proven non-vacuous: reordering compose-up.sh so the cap installs after
   `systemctl enable --now docker` fails both.
 - test_observability_docker_storage.py:232-253 — an unrecognised size in a row the ledger
   SUMS still fails closed (a ledger that under-reports would inflate the residue and page for
   accounted bytes), but an unrecognised ROW TYPE is now ignored rather than fatal, so a
   future engine adding a fifth row cannot silently take the incident metric off the air.

## file_impact UNCHANGED

Exactly the same 10 declared paths; no file added, so the signed plan-review attestation
stands and no re-review is forced.

## Verification

make lint 0 (complexity new=0 increased=0; mechanism new=0 increased=0 — no marker needed,
the detectors scan src/ and scripts/, not infra/). make typecheck 0 (763 files).
terraform fmt -check -recursive 0; init -backend=false + validate Success. NO TERRAFORM
APPLIED. Blast-radius suite — every test file referencing observability.sh, compose-up.sh,
monitoring_autodeploy.tf or review-bot-ops.md, plus test_autodeploy_prune.py — 550 passed,
20 skipped, 0 failures. The three pytest-only gates run clean: test_mechanism_delta and
test_api_surface_gate 49 passed, test_predates_gate_guard_parity 6 passed.

`make verify` did NOT complete: the harness killed it at the wall-clock limit while three
other full suites were running concurrently on this host. Its pytest died with it — no
orphan. The selections above are what stands in for it.

Host hygiene: check_orphaned_load.py flagged a leaked `zsh -c trap 'kill 0' EXIT INT TERM;
sleep 1` at PPID 1, 94% CPU, 61 CPU-minutes on a one-second sleep. Not from this session, but
it was poisoning every timing-sensitive measurement on the box including three live suites.
Confirmed sole member of its own process group, then reaped; the detector is clean.
